text:
jess: quick heads-up — I'm seeing a perf regression on SM90 for the fused+paged FlashAttention path after the KV-paging heuristic change. ms/token up ~25% for longseq workloads (seq=2k, batch=1).
ryan: yikes. which kernel build? Triton or hand-written CUDA?
jess: Triton 2.1 build using flash_paged variant (we switched default selector to prefer paged for low-RSS hosts). CUDA runtime is 12.4.
hao: can you paste the perf numbers and a tiny profiling dump?
jess: sure — quick numbers:
```
model=gpt-3.8b seq=2048 batch=1
SM80 (CUDA12.1, native CUDA kernels): 12.1 ms/step (~830 tok/s)
SM90 (CUDA12.4, Triton flash_paged): 15.2 ms/step (~660 tok/s)
previous SM90 (CUDA12.1, cuda-flash-fused): 12.5 ms/step (~800 tok/s)
```
ryan: so SM90 + Triton combo seems slower than either SM80 or SM90 native CUDA. indicates kernel generation/tiling mismatch.
tara: did the paging policy change also alter the KV coalescing or prefix caching behavior? even small changes there can shift mem access patterns a lot.
jess: yes — new heuristic defers materializing large contiguous KV pages until warm; it increases scattered page hits early. could be hurting vectorized loads in the Triton kernels.
perf-bot: profiler snapshot (nvprof-like):
```
GPU 0: kernel flash_paged_attention_grid (triton): avg 9.6 ms (mem stalls 48%)
GPU 0: kernel fused_qkv_cuda (native): avg 3.4 ms (mem stalls 22%)
```
indicates memory-bound on Triton kernel.
hao: that matches: Triton-generated kernels may not be picking the optimal vector width for SM90 (fp16/float8 lanes changed), causing worse global memory coalescing.
ryan: can you repro with env var TRITON_DISABLE_AUTOTUNER=1 to force conservative kernel choices? also try CUDA 12.1 on same SM90 machine to rule out driver changes.
jess: reproducer running now. also testing toggling KV paging back to old heuristic.
(later) jess: quick update — forcing TRITON_DISABLE_AUTOTUNER=1 recovers most perf (13.0 ms/step). switching KV paging back also recovers (12.6 ms). both together -> 12.4 ms (parity).
tara: ok so 2 factors: Triton autotuner picks bad kernel configs on SM90 with current tiling heuristics; KV paging heuristic increases scatter pattern causing autotuner to prefer different kernel shape.
linda: do we have CI perf tests to catch this earlier? maybe a cross-arch benchmark matrix (SM80/SM90) with Triton vs CUDA baseline for key seq lengths.
hao: we have nightly perf runners but not covering paged attention + low-RSS heuristics. we should add a small matrix: {seq:512,1024,2048} x {batch:1,2} x {SM80,SM90} x {triton,cuda} and flag >10% regressions.
ryan: plan proposal: 1) revert default selector to prefer native CUDA fused for SM90 until Triton autotuner fixes; 2) push KV paging tweak that preserves contiguous page materialization for first N steps (avoid scatter transient); 3) file issue with Triton team (include perf traces + device-specific tile sizes).
jess: I can prepare a condensed perf diff and attach nvprof traces for the issue. assigning to hao to open the Triton ticket (they want kernel config reproducible).
hao: on it. I'll include minimal repro, env, and a small binary kernel dump.
tara: also add a short note in rollout doc: "paged-KV is opt-in for now on SM90 until autotuner / heuristics validated".
ryan: reminder — for Dedicated customers we should fall back to verified kernel variants automatically when we detect >15% perf regression in 5m window. add to routing rules.
jess: filed a short PR draft to change selector and a follow-up to add perf matrix. PTAL @team. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: perf-alert: added benchmark job 1773002468 to perf-ci queue; will run cross-arch matrix overnight.
linda: thanks everyone. good triage. once Triton ticket lands let's sync and schedule a canary.
